av_event.line_text: Erm, honestly? Targets. Head office want the figures up every month, and I lie awake thinking about it sometimes. And complaints. I had a landlord ring me at nine o'clock on a Sunday night about a dripping tap. On a Sunday!
av_event.what: A phone on the desk just below the camera lights up the lower edge of the frame. Tomasz looks down at it for about two seconds, reaches out of shot, and the glow disappears as he turns it face down. Then he looks back at the camera.

text:
B: Hi, hello! Can you hear me okay?
A: Yes. I am Tomasz, I'm in Reading.
B: Gemma, I'm in Maidstone, in Kent. So, erm, what is it you do?
A: Student. Construction Management, second year at University of Reading. Before that I was team leader at a warehouse, six years.
B: Oh, construction, right. My husband's an electrician, he runs his own business, so I hear a lot about site managers. Mostly moaning, to be fair. I'm a branch manager at a lettings agency, I've got a team of five, so I'm dealing with contractors all day as well. Plumbers, gas engineers, all that.
A: Okay. Are they reliable?
B: Some of them. Some of them I wouldn't trust to change a lightbulb, honestly. You chase them, they say Tuesday, they turn up Friday, and then the tenant's on the phone to me.
A: Same at warehouse. If a driver says nine, he means eleven. You plan for eleven.
B: Ha, yeah, that's exactly it. You learn, don't you?
A: Yes.
B: So are you renting, or have you bought, or...?
A: Renting. Two-bedroom flat in Earley, with my wife. To be honest, the flat is cold. I do my reading in the library now because of it.
B: Oh, that's not good. Has the landlord done anything about it? Because if it's the heating, or the windows, that's on them, you know? Have you reported it in writing?
A: Sorry, what do you mean exactly? In writing to the agent, or the landlord?
B: To whoever manages it. Email, so there's a record. If it's an agent, they've got to pass it on. I'd be on that straight away if it was one of mine. The good agents are, anyway. Sorry, work mode.
A: No, that's useful. I will email. We want to buy anyway, Woodley or Wokingham, after I graduate.
B: Wokingham's not cheap, mind. Woodley you've probably got a better chance, some of the older semis come up. My advice, get your deposit sorted and your mortgage in principle before you even look, because the good ones go in a weekend.
A: I have a spreadsheet already. Deposit, stamp duty, solicitor, survey.
B: Course you have. You looked organised in your photo, with the big planner.
A: It helps. What is hardest in your job?
B: Erm, honestly? Targets. Head office want the figures up every month, and I lie awake thinking about it sometimes. And complaints. I had a landlord ring me at nine o'clock on a Sunday night about a dripping tap. On a Sunday!
A: Did you answer?
B: I did, yeah, which was my mistake. Now he thinks he can. Do you get stressed, with the uni stuff?
A: Not with my own work. With group project, yes. One person has not done his part. I am not happy.
B: Oh, I'd be the same, I can't stand people who don't pull their weight. I've got one in my team like that, I'm always having to chase. Sorry, am I going on?
A: No. It's fine.
B: So what do you do at the weekend, to switch off?
A: This weekend, brake pads on my car. Skoda Octavia. I do it myself, it's much cheaper than a garage.
B: See, Dean would love you. He does all ours, and then he tells everyone how much he saved, every single...
